# voice-restore

> Forensic + editorial skill: determine whether an English text was AI-polished, then
> restore the author's own writing fingerprint (rather than a generic "human" average).

## What it is for

- "Is this document AI-touched?"
- "My essay was flagged; make it sound like me again"
- "Find the paragraphs that were uniformly rewritten"

## Core claim

Sentence-shape metrics (length variance, short-sentence ratio, opener distribution) measure
how *smoothed* a text is, not whether a model wrote it. A non-native writer is flat by
default; flat is their fingerprint. Optimising toward "average human writing" makes them
less like themselves.

## Three forensic tells

1. First-person count across a long document (zero is deletion, not restraint)
2. Prose semicolons (exclude table footnotes and citation separators)
3. `the` vs `this` sentence-initial split (ratio matters more than either value)

## Procedure

Phase 1 forensics -> Phase 2 personal baseline -> Phase 3 restore (syntax, then vocabulary,
then verify). Vocabulary must be re-measured after syntax: rebuilding sentences tempts you
to add `therefore` and `rather than`, which are the strongest LLM-academic markers.

## CLI

    python scripts/voice_metrics.py report sample.txt
    python scripts/voice_metrics.py compare baseline.txt draft.txt

Standard library only. Python 3.8+.

## Files

- SKILL.md — the procedure
- references/case-notes.md — one full case with measured numbers and three corrections
- scripts/voice_metrics.py — measurement
